Hebrew, naha, nehi, nihyah, the repetition representing the continuous and monotonous wail.<div eID="gen23580" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23581" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he hath changed the portion of my people--</hi>a charge of injustice against Jehovah. He transfers to other nations the sacred territory assigned as the rightful portion of our people (<reference osisRef="Mic.1.15">Mi 1:15</reference>).<div eID="gen23581" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23582" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">turning away he hath divided our fields--</hi>Turning away from us to the enemy, He hath divided among them our fields. Calvin, as the Margin, explains, "Instead of restoring our territory, He hath divided our fields among our enemies, each of whom henceforward will have an interest in keeping what he hath gotten: so that we are utterly shut out from hope of restoration." So "backsliding," that is, backslider (<reference osisRef="Jer.49.4">Jr 49:4</reference>). English Version gives a good sense; and is quite tenable in the Hebrew. <div eID="gen23582" type="x-p"/>

Therefore--</hi>resumed from <reference osisRef="Mic.2.3">Mi 2:3</reference>. On account of your crimes described in <reference osisRef="Mic.2.1">Mi 2:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.2">2</reference>.<div eID="gen23583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23584" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thou--</hi>the ideal individual ("me," <reference osisRef="Mic.2.4">Mi 2:4</reference>), representing the guilty people in whose name he spoke.<div eID="gen23584" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23585" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">none that ... cast a cord by lot--</hi>none who shall have any possession measured out.<div eID="gen23585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23586" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the congregation of the Lord--</hi>among the people consecrated to Jehovah. This is God's implied answer to their complaint of injustice (<reference osisRef="Mic.2.4">Mi 2:4</reference>). <div eID="gen23586" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12736"/><div sID="gen23587" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12736"/><hi type="bold">6. Prophesy ye not, say they--</hi>namely, the Israelites say to the true prophets, when announcing unwelcome truths. Therefore God judicially abandons them to their own ways: "The prophets, by whose ministry they might have been saved from shame (ignominious captivity), shall not (that is, no longer) prophesy to them" (<reference osisRef="Isa.30.10">Is 30:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.2.12">Am 2:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.7.16">7:16</reference>). Maurer translates the latter clause, "they shall not prophesy of such things" (as in <reference osisRef="Mic.2.3-Mic.2.5">Mi 2:3-5</reference>, these being rebellious Israel's words); "let them not prophesy"; "they never cease from insult" (from prophesying insults to us). English Version is supported by the parallelism: wherein the similarity of sound and word implies how exactly God makes their punishment answer to their sin, and takes them at their own word. "Prophesy," literally, "drop" (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.2">De 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.2">Eze 21:2</reference>). <div eID="gen23587" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12737"/><div sID="gen23588" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12737"/><hi type="bold">7. O thou ... named the house of Jacob--</hi>priding thyself on the name, though having naught of the spirit, of thy progenitor. Also, bearing the name which ought to remind thee of God's favors granted to thee because of His covenant with Jacob.<div eID="gen23588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23589" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">is the Spirit of the Lord straitened?--</hi>Is His compassion contracted within narrower limits now than formerly, so that He should delight in your destruction (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.77.7-Ps.77.9">Psa 77:7-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.59.1">Is 59:1</reference>, 2)?<div eID="gen23589" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23590" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">are these his doings?--</hi>that is, Are such threatenings His delight? Ye dislike the prophets' threatenings (<reference osisRef="Mic.2.6">Mi 2:6</reference>): but who is to blame? Not God, for He delights in blessing, rather than threatening; but yourselves (<reference osisRef="Mic.2.8">Mi 2:8</reference>) who provoke His threatenings [Grotius]. Calvin translates, "Are your doings such as are prescribed by Him?" Ye boast of being God's peculiar people: Do ye then conform your lives to God's law?<div eID="gen23590" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23591" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly--</hi>Are not My words good to the upright? If your ways were upright, My words would not be threatening (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.18.26">Psa 18:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.11.19">Mt 11:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.7.17">Joh 7:17</reference>). <div eID="gen23591" type="x-p"/>

The women of my people--</hi>that is, the widows of the men slain by you (<reference osisRef="Mic.2.2">Mi 2:2</reference>) ye cast out from their homes which had been their delight, and seize on them for yourselves.<div eID="gen23597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23598" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from their children--</hi>that is, from the orphans of the widows.<div eID="gen23598" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23599" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">taken away my glory--</hi>namely, their substance and raiment, which, being the fruit of God's blessing on the young, reflected God's glory. Thus Israel's crime was not merely robbery, but sacrilege. Their sex did not save the women, nor their age the children from violence.<div eID="gen23599" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23600" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for ever--</hi>There was no repentance. They persevered in sin. The pledged garment was to be restored to the poor before sunset (<reference osisRef="Exod.22.26">Ex 22:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.22.27">27</reference>); but these never restored their unlawful booty. <div eID="gen23600" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 9. The women of my people-- that is, the widows of the men slain by you ( Mi 2:2 ) ye cast out from their homes which had been their delight, and seize on them for yourselves. from their children-- that is, from the orphans of the widows. taken away my glory-- namely, their substance and raiment, which, being the fruit of God's blessing on the young, reflected God's glory. Thus Israel's crime was not merely robbery, but sacrilege. Their sex did not save the women, nor their age the children from violence. for ever-- There was no repentance. They persevered in sin. The pledged garment was to be restored to the poor before sunset ( Ex 22:26 , 27 ); but these never restored their unlawful booty.
entries.reader_content_plain: 9. The women of my people-- that is, the widows of the men slain by you ( Mi 2:2 ) ye cast out from their homes which had been their delight, and seize on them for yourselves. from their children-- that is, from the orphans of the widows. taken away my glory-- namely, their substance and raiment, which, being the fruit of God's blessing on the young, reflected God's glory. Thus Israel's crime was not merely robbery, but sacrilege. Their sex did not save the women, nor their age the children from violence. for ever-- There was no repentance. They persevered in sin. The pledged garment was to be restored to the poor before sunset ( Ex 22:26 , 27 ); but these never restored their unlawful booty.

A sudden transition from threats to the promise of a glorious restoration. Compare a similar transition in <reference osisRef="Hos.1.9">Ho 1:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.10">10</reference>. Jehovah, too, prophesies of good things to come, but not like the false prophets, "of wine and strong drink" (<reference osisRef="Mic.2.11">Mi 2:11</reference>). After I have sent you into captivity as I have just threatened, I will thence assemble you again (compare <reference osisRef="Mic.4.6">Mi 4:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">7</reference>).<div eID="gen23605" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23606" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all of thee--</hi>The restoration from Babylon was partial. Therefore that here meant must be still future, when "all Israel shall be saved" (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Ro 11:26</reference>). Israel--</hi>the ten tribes' kingdom (<reference osisRef="Hos.12.2">Ho 12:2</reference>) and Judah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.19.8">2Ch 19:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.21.2">21:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.21.4">4</reference>).<div eID="gen23607" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23608" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">remnant--</hi>the elect remnant, which shall survive the previous calamities of Judah, and from which the nation is to spring into new life (<reference osisRef="Isa.6.13">Is 6:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.10.20-Isa.10.22">10:20-22</reference>).<div eID="gen23608" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23609" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as the sheep of Bozrah--</hi>a region famed for its rich pastures (compare <reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.4">2Ki 3:4</reference>). Gesenius for Bozrah translates, "sheepfold." But thus there will be tautology unless the next clause be translated, "in the midst of their pasture." entries.content_plain: 13. The breaker-- Jehovah-Messiah, who breaks through every obstacle in the way of their restoration: not as formerly breaking forth to destroy them for transgression ( Ex 19:22 ; Jud 21:15 ), but breaking a way for them through their enemies. they-- the returning Israelites and Jews. passed through the gate-- that is, through the gate of the foe's city in which they had been captives. So the image of the resurrection ( Ho 13:14 ) represents Israel's restoration. their king-- "the Breaker," peculiarly "their king" ( Ho 3:5 ; Mt 27:37 ). pass before them-- as He did when they went up out of Egypt ( Ex 13:21 ; De 1:30 , 33). the Lord on the head of them-- Jehovah at their head ( Is 52:12 ). Messiah, the second person, is meant (compare Ex 23:20 ; 33:14 ; Is 63:9 ).
